The h6 case fails. `strings.Index("###### This will be an h6", " ")` = 6. My condition `level < 6` fails for level=6. It should be `level <= 6`. h1 → level 1, h6 → level 6, h7 → level 7. So the condition should be `level <= 6`, or equivalently `level < 7`.

Done. Let me summarize the refactoring.

Done — all 17 test cases pass and `go vet` is clean. ## What the refactoring did The original `Render` was a single ~80-line loop that scanned the document character by character, juggling five intertwined state variables (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`, `pos`) with several hard-to-follow tricks (e.g. `pos += 2` to skip a list marker, `strings.LastIndex` comparisons to decide when to close a list, a global emphasis pass before parsing). The rewrite in `markdown.go` replaces that with line-oriented parsing: - **`Render`** splits the document on newlines and dispatches each line by prefix: `#` → header, `* ` → list item, anything else → paragraph. A single `inList` flag plus a `closeList` helper manage the `
    `/`
` wrapping. - **`renderHeader`** derives the header level from the position of the first space — 1–6 hashes become ``, seven or more fall through to a paragraph (preserving the original "h7 is a paragraph" behavior). - **`renderParagraph`** wraps a line in `

…

`. - **`renderEmphasis`** keeps the original's exact semantics: replace exactly one pair of `__…__` and one pair of `_…_` markers, which is what makes the mixed-emphasis test (`This will _be_ __mixed__`) produce correctly ordered output. One bug I caught while writing it: my first draft used `level < 6` for the header check, which misclassified h6 (first space at index 6) as a paragraph — fixed to `level <= 6`. `markdown_test.go` and `cases_test.go` were not modified, and no new files were created.
